catalog_row.Наименование: Проводная клавиатура для ПК Alloy Rise 75 (Red switch) (RU)

keyboard.discovery_method: Found via https://hyperx.com/collections/gaming-keyboards, an already-known nav link from the microphone product page fixture -- not guessed.

identity_check.mismatch_detail: Catalog row names this the (RU) market variant (suffix #ACB). The fetched official page's own additionalProperty explicitly states 'Keyboard Layout: US Layout' and its offer name reads 'HyperX Alloy Rise 75 – Mechanical Gaming Keyboard - Black / US Layout / HyperX Red - Linear' -- suffix #ABA. Same base model code (7G7A4AA), different regional/layout suffix. This is a real, evidenced identity GAP, not a confirmed match -- no RU-specific hyperx.com page was found, and none was guessed to paper over the gap.

mouse.discovery_method: Found via https://hyperx.com/collections/gaming-mice, an already-known nav link from the microphone product page fixture -- not guessed.

identity_json_ld_sku_field.shape_present_and_stable: confirmed on all 3 live-fetched pages (microphone, keyboard, mouse) -- same signature match to Stage 8.1's original contract

value_matches_catalog_row_exactly.keyboard_7G7A4AA: base code only -- exact suffix mismatch (US vs RU layout variant)

identity_json_ld_sku_field.conclusion: The FIELD is a compatible_primitive (present, stable shape, 3/3 pages). Whether its VALUE matches a given catalog row exactly is NOT guaranteed by the field existing -- it must be checked per catalog row, per market. 2 of 3 checked rows matched exactly; one did not, for a real, identified reason (regional layout variant).

specifications_additionalProperty_json_l.conclusion: The additionalProperty FIELD is present on all 3 pages (compatible_primitive shape). Its VALUE population is NOT reliable across pages -- fully empty on the microphone, partially populated on the mouse, mostly populated on the keyboard. This must be checked live per page; a shared reader cannot assume non-empty values just because the field exists.

specifications_dom_table_fallback.note: specs-label/specs-value <td> pairs inside a <table>, not literally Stage 8.1's abstracted "dl:dt+dd"/"accordion" labels, but functionally the same role.
specifications_dom_table_fallback.conclusion: This DOM table is the reliably-populated specification source on all 3 pages sampled -- confirmed compatible_primitive at both shape AND value level, unlike the JSON-LD additionalProperty reader above.

largest_advertised_size_by_page.mouse: 1500x1500 (via Product.image) -- genuinely smaller; not upscaled or guessed

media_json_ld_image_field.conclusion: compatible_primitive -- reliable on all 3 pages, real dimensions each time, no invented CDN transforms.

media_dom_responsive_srcset.CORRECTION_to_stage8_1_characterization: On all 3 live-fetched pages, every srcset attribute containing a real comma-separated multi-width list belongs to the shared site theme logo image (hyperxlogo_150x.svg / _300x.svg), never to a product photo. Every product-photo srcset/src attribute is a SINGLE URL, not a responsive width list. Stage 8.1's "responsive_srcset" DOM marker fires because the attribute exists somewhere on the page, but it does not describe genuine per-product responsive images. The actually reliable size signal is the JSON-LD image.width/height, not this DOM marker.

documents.conclusion: insufficient_evidence to claim documents are ever exposed via a PDF link on hyperx.com product pages -- a stable, now 5-page-wide, negative finding. Not claimed as proof no HyperX product page anywhere has one.
